title: Triple
content: A triple is a single fact expressed as a subject, a predicate, and an object, the unit that knowledge graphs use to store relationships.

meta.why: A sentence that states the subject, the relationship, and the value in plain order reads as one fact.
meta.example: The statement that Acme Software has its headquarters in Denver contains the subject Acme Software, the predicate has headquarters in, and the object Denver.
meta.check: Review key facts about your company and rewrite sentences whose subject is a vague pronoun so each fact names its subject.
meta.limitation: The triple is a data model from the W3C RDF specification, and writing in subject, predicate, object order does not add a fact to a knowledge graph.
meta.sources: W3C: RDF 1.1 Primer | https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-primer/ | Standards specification
